note: _loadRealFacades (citymap.js:6241-6280): the facades.json manifest reader, the ten apply() bindings in source order, the 1/bays x 1/floors tiling, the per-kind anisotropy split (16x for panel/glass/panel2/tower16/khrush5, 8x for the rest) and the roofs.json race guard. This was a real hole, not a refinement: roofs.json, walls.json, loggia_tiles.json and textures/pb/manifest.json all already had readers, but a grep for 'facades.json' across Assets/Scripts and Assets/Editor found NONE, so the eight real photographed Tbilisi wall tiles were never applied and every one of those walls silently fell back to a procedural tile. The assets were already imported (Assets/Art/Textures/facades/ holds both the .jpg files and facades.json). NOT claimed: binding the Texture2D objects to the live shared materials at load time, which belongs to City/CityMaterials.cs (the one place that turns a manifest key into a bound texture); this class supplies the decision data it needs. The roof pair is deliberately kept out of Bindings and gated behind ShouldApplyRoofPair, because citymap.js:6270-6271 says applying it here as well would race build_roof_materials.py's own loader.
verified: unity/Assets/Editor/Probes/RealFacadeProbe.cs vs tools/_probe_realfacades.mjs, RUN and diffed: PASS, 61 values across 35/35 paired lines at float32 precision. The .mjs reads the REAL public/textures/facades/facades.json and regexes the apply() call list out of the REAL _loadRealFacades body, so the bindings, the per-kind anisotropy and the 1/bays x 1/floors tiling are checked against shipped data rather than a retyped copy: BINDING_COUNT=10 (eight wall targets plus the two conditional roof ones, each with its JS target expression), every tiling pair (glass 7 bays x 8 floors -> 0.142857,0.125; tower16 5 x 14 -> 0.2,0.071429), ROOFPAIR_GUARDED=true, MANIFEST_KINDS=28, and CREDITS_MISSING=0 across all ten. That last one is a LICENCE check rather than a cosmetic one: these are CC BY / CC BY-SA photographs and a missing credit is an obligation unmet.
